runners_data.name: Nyman
runners_data.note: Won on soft over 7f recently (6 days ago), steps up to 8f where it has placed previously; midfield style suits a contested gallop, neutral draw in 9, trainer Roger Fell in fair form (T14: 3/20).

runners_data.name: Masaban
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's top pick at low confidence; confirmed front-runner drawn 10 (neutral) who must fight for the lead with Clatford — has a soft-ground place and an 8f win in recent form but facing genuine early pressure makes the confidence rider appropriate.

runners_data.name: Berry Clever
runners_data.note: Consistent place-getter at this level but has not won in six runs, all finishing 4th-5th range; midfield style and draw 6 are acceptable but the flat recent form string (454444) is hard to get excited about.

runners_data.name: Bella Bisbee
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with the significant advantage of draw 5 in the favoured low section; trainer Scott Dixon winless in last 20 (T14: 0/20) is a real flag, and the form string (502836) is patchy — the draw helps but the yard angle tempers enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Celtic Chariot
runners_data.note: Strand Scorecard danger; back-to-back wins over 8f on good ground and a favoured draw in stall 1 give this 3-year-old an outstanding tactical position; Adrian Nicholls rides and the trainer is in fair nick (T14: 3/17) — the profile fits the likely race shape well.

runners_data.name: Clatford
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner drawn 2 (favoured), but has had 85 days off and the form string is only three runs deep (420); Scott Dixon's yard is 0 from 20 over 14 days — the pace role is genuine but the fitness and trainer angle are significant concerns.

runners_data.name: Little Miss India
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse wearing headgear, but drawn 4 in the favoured section; last ran 140 days ago which is a notable layoff, and recent form at shorter trips and longer distances than today's mile makes the profile awkward — the return from absence is the headline worry.

runners_data.name: Espona Bay
runners_data.note: Prominent-style 3-year-old drawn against in stall 15; has winning form at 7f and placed at 8f but the wide draw on a track where low numbers are favoured costs it materially — Scott Dixon yard (0/20) adds a second negative.

runners_data.name: Wield
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with tongue-tie, drawn 3 (favoured); has placed at 8f on standard going but the form string (325072) shows inconsistency and a poor last run — the draw is genuinely useful and Joe Fanning's experience is a positive in a tricky pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Shadow Run
runners_data.note: Naturally a hold-up horse, though placed in the midfield section of the map because the field's high density of hold-up types leaves it racing somewhat out of its preferred role — its soft-going run of 6th at 8f and Scott Dixon's 0/20 T14 make this hard to recommend regardless of shape.

runners_data.name: Serious Look
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with recent form over 10-12f; dropping to a mile today is a trip shortening that may not suit a staying type, drawn against in 14 — best hope is a truly extreme pace that sets up a late run from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Caragio
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse drawn against in 11 after a 89-day absence; trainer-jockey combination of Adam Kirby has limited recent data (T14: 0/5) and the last run over 8f on standard going was a distant 6th — hard to make a case here.

runners_data.name: Tolstoy
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type in stall 12 (against), with headgear; recent form (54000) is deeply discouraging and the soft-going record of one place from eight runs is a real concern — sim-going figures suggest little ability to handle today's conditions.

runners_data.name: Anthropologist
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing headgear (P), drawn neutral in 8; placed twice at 7f on standard going but the soft-going record is just one place from 15 runs — Sammy Jo Bell rides for the in-form Herrington yard (T14: 3/18) which is the main positive.

runners_data.name: Quiet Resolve
runners_data.note: Prominent runner drawn against in 16; has placed at 8f on good and soft-ish ground with Gay Kelleway aboard — the wide draw on a track strongly favouring low numbers is a serious tactical hurdle to overcome regardless of ability.

runners_data.name: Feel The Need
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse reassigned to midfield on the map because there are more genuine rear-runners than the shape can place; the yard is in form (Herrington T14: 3/18) but Feel The Need's own record is poor (0 wins, recent 7th/6th/13th) and racing ahead of its natural position further diminishes the chance.

races.paceDynamic: Clatford and Masaban are the two confirmed front-runners, and with both drawn in the favoured low numbers (2 and 10 respectively), they will push for the lead from the off, creating a genuinely contested gallop on soft ground over a mile — not a dawdle. Shadow Run and Feel The Need are natural hold-up horses but are mapped to midfield because the field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; Clatford and Masaban are most likely to actually secure the front positions, with Celtic Chariot and Bella Bisbee — both prominent-style runners in the favoured low draws — tracking closely behind them. The honest, contested pace on softish ground over a mile will stretch the field and make this a thorough test of stamina, burning off horses who get into a scrimmage early and do not truly see out the trip. This race shape strongly favours prominent or mid-division horses with proven soft-ground stamina who can save a little for the closing stages — pure pace-dependent runners or those racing out of their natural position face the biggest discount.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Clatford and Masaban fight it out in front and the honest gallop on soft ground sets up a race for prominent-tracking types.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners push along at a genuine clip, softening up the leaders, and a prominent horse who tracks at close range pounces in the final two furlongs; Celtic Chariot's favoured draw (1), proven form on good-to-soft, and back-to-back course wins at 8f make it the profile that benefits most here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Masaban Controls, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Masaban is allowed to dictate from the front and the pace is honest but not brutal, with Clatford unable to sustain the challenge.
scenarios.body: Masaban secures the rail and finds a soft lead once Clatford gets outpaced or backs off, setting a rhythm it can maintain; its soft-ground win at 8f and prior proximity form give it the profile to hold on as others fail to close.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Hosts Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the pace burns brightly enough that front-runners tie each other up and the race develops into a classic front-pace collapse.
scenarios.body: A horse tracking in midfield with genuine soft-ground stamina picks up the pieces in the closing furlong; Nyman's soft-going win at 7f, recency (6 days), and step up to 8f gives it the profile, while Wield (draw 3, favoured) has the course position to exploit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly scorching and the entire front group collapses, leaving a well-back horse to pick up in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: This scenario is materially discounted because the natural hold-up horses — Shadow Run and Feel The Need — have been redistributed to midfield and are not operating in their true role, reducing the chance of a genuine late-closing surge from deep; Serious Look or Caragio would need a perfect storm.

watchPoints.text: Watch Celtic Chariot (draw 1) — if it settles just off the front-running battle between Clatford and Masaban, its back-to-back 8f wins and favoured draw make it the most dangerous horse in the race.

Watch Clatford's early sections closely — if it fails to match Masaban's pace or shows any sign of ring-rustiness after 85 days off, the entire front-end dynamic changes and prominent trackers gain an even larger advantage.

Scott Dixon has three runners (Bella Bisbee, Clatford, Espona Bay) and is 0 from 20 over the last 14 days — if the yard is in a cold spell, all three should be downgraded regardless of their individual profiles.

Little Miss India returns after 140 days off; monitor in the ring and early stages for signs it is not fully wound up, as a first-time-back flat performance over what may be a non-ideal trip could mislead future assessors.

The favoured low draws are stacked with competitive runners (Celtic Chariot 1, Clatford 2, Wield 3, Little Miss India 4, Bella Bisbee 5) — watch for potential crowding on the rail in the early stages if all track the inside line simultaneously.

races.paceDynamic: Caballo De Mar is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger likely to press him hard from flag to flag over 2m2f on soft ground, he should be able to control a measured, sustainable gallop from the front. Queenstown, Berkshire Sundance, and Ascending are all natural prominent types, but with Winday and Ascending redistributed to midfield on the map because the field is too front-heavy for all to occupy their preferred berth, it is Caballo De Mar and Berkshire Sundance who are most likely to actually lock down the early positions, with Queenstown tracking just behind. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than this race shape can accommodate cleanly — Ascending and Winday are genuine pace horses who will be forced to sit further back than they would like, compromising their chance in a scenario that requires them to be handy. On soft ground over a testing 2m2f flat Doncaster trip, a controlled front-running tempo with a late sustained gallop strongly favours prominent racers who can travel smoothly just behind the leader and produce a long, grinding finish — making the prominent-to-midfield profile the one to side with.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Caballo De Mar sets a measured but not suicidal gallop and Queenstown tracks efficiently in his slipstream throughout.
scenarios.body: Caballo De Mar dictates from the front at a pace that suits the conditions, but the soft ground and marathon trip ensure the finish is a test of stamina rather than speed, benefiting horses who travel prominently and sustain their effort; Queenstown, lobbing along just behind on going that suits, is ideally placed to challenge in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Caballo De Mar, given a completely uncontested lead, finds the soft ground no obstacle and simply stays on too strongly for his rivals.
scenarios.body: With no one willing or able to apply pressure early, Caballo De Mar dictates every fraction and preserves enough energy to repel late challengers in a race run entirely to his tempo; his soft-going form is limited but the uncontested lead could compensate for that question mark.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong early and the prominent horses tie each other up, leaving something for the hold-up brigade.
scenarios.body: Peace Belle and Beylerbeyi, operating from the back, would need a strong enough gallop to bring them into the picture in the final two furlongs, and soft ground does give hold-up horses a fighting chance if the leaders have burned their reserves; Peace Belle's soft-ground placed form gives her the best credentials here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Scramble, Unexpected
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types battle for position early, unsettling the gallop and producing an unusually tactical contest over the trip.
scenarios.body: Redistributed pace horses Ascending and Winday fighting for better ground than the map allows could create a muddling, stop-start rhythm that scrambles the form book; in that chaos, a horse like Epic Poet, sitting midfield with clean air, could pick up the pieces if rivals have burned too much energy jostling for position.

watchPoints.text: Queenstown's ability to travel smoothly just off Caballo De Mar's pace is the key tactical moment — if Ryan Moore can't get that position cleanly by halfway, his challenge could be compromised.
Ascending and Winday are both natural pace horses being forced further back than ideal — watch the first half-mile for any scrimmaging as they are displaced from their preferred spots.
Caballo De Mar's soft-going record (0W0P in similar conditions) is a genuine flag — if the ground proves more testing than Good to Soft, his tendency to fade late could be accelerated.
Berkshire Sundance returns from 42 days off; watch his early behavioural signs and whether Andrew Balding has him tuned up sufficiently after that break to challenge in a Group 2.
Peace Belle's hold-up style means she needs the pace to be genuinely strong — if Caballo De Mar crawls, she will never get competitive in the straight and her each-way appeal evaporates entirely.

races.paceDynamic: Nochebuena and Golden Muse are confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead, creating a genuine, honest gallop from the outset over 1m4f on Good to Soft ground at Doncaster. With two willing pace-setters pushing each other along, the tempo is unlikely to collapse into a crawl, and the ground will ensure the gallop bites into stamina reserves from a relatively early stage. The resulting scenario — a genuine pace, strung-out field, and a premium on finishing effort rather than tactical speed — is one that classically rewards hold-up horses with a proven stamina profile who can pick up the pieces once the front two begin to tire. Midfield-to-hold-up runners with confirmed soft-ground form and the ability to sustain a run from two furlongs out are the profile that this race shape most directly favours.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Nochebuena and Golden Muse push each other along and the honest gallop exposes the front-runners before the home straight.
scenarios.body: The two pace-setters soften each other up, and the hold-up horses tracking comfortably in mid-division are able to peel out and deliver sustained late runs on ground that rewards stamina over speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Splits Honours
scenarios.trigger: If Nochebuena or Golden Muse manages to control the pace solo after the other capitulates early, leaving a well-judged front-running display.
scenarios.body: One front-runner dictates from a position of comfort rather than duress, with the field unable to reel them in on easy ground; the pace-setter who gets the better of the early duel and settles best would have the significant advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly unrelenting and reduces the race to a stamina test where class and consistency over a mile and four furlongs is decisive.
scenarios.body: Horses with proven form at this trip and in similar conditions pick their way through a spent field in the final two furlongs; the premium falls on those with the most reliable staying profile at this distance.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Early, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners surprisingly ease off each other and the pace collapses into a falsely-run race with a sharp finish.
scenarios.body: The race compresses into a sprint from two furlongs out, favouring horses with the speed to quicken from a mid-pack position rather than pure stayers; this is the least likely shape given two confirmed lead-seekers are present.

watchPoints.text: Golden Muse has never raced on turf or ground with cut — if the Good to Soft surface blunts her early zip, Nochebuena could inherit an uncontested lead and the entire pace scenario shifts markedly.

Aequitas returns from 307 days off the track with deteriorating AW form and no recent turf evidence — if she outperforms expectations she could disrupt the midfield pattern, but the lay-off is a severe risk flag.
Room Fourteen's appeal as a Strand scorecard danger rests on form entirely built on Good ground — if the Good to Soft is on the testing side of that description, her chance is genuinely compromised.

Green Sky carries a 7lb claim via Charlie Tucker, which partially offsets her 0-from-3 record on similar going — watch whether that weight advantage allows her to travel more comfortably than her soft-ground figures suggest.

Both Nochebuena and Golden Muse jumping from draws 2 and 10 respectively means early position-taking will be visible immediately — if one backs off inside the first two furlongs, monitor which hold-up horse immediately begins to travel most smoothly through the pack.

runners_data.name: Fern Clyde
runners_data.note: Placed form over multiple trips and going types, including a win over 6f on good; Tim Easterby's yard is active (17/99) and Duran Fentiman knows the horse; from stall 16 and wearing headgear (ht), she is genuinely a front-runner by inclination but will be unable to secure that position against five confirmed pace horses — the wide draw and pace scenario push her into a role that doesn't suit her natural profile.

races.paceDynamic: Pride Of Toledo, Wait Geordie, Beresford Gap, Sir Sirius, and Sue's Last Chance all want to be on or near the pace, guaranteeing a strong, contested early gallop over 6f on Good to Soft ground at Doncaster — a flat track where soft conditions will stretch stamina reserves and expose those who burn fuel early. With five confirmed front-runners fighting for position, the race is likely to be run at a searching tempo from the outset, compressing the field and creating a genuinely gruelling test that will favour horses who travel smoothly just off the pace and finish with purpose rather than those who have had to scrap for position or lead from the front. The field contains more pace-biased horses than can realistically claim a prominent berth — Fern Clyde and Fasthope are naturally prominent types who are displaced into midfield on the map because Pride Of Toledo, Wait Geordie, Beresford Gap, Sir Sirius, and Sue's Last Chance will dominate the early positions; Fern Clyde from stall 16 and Fasthope from 15 may find themselves shuffled back further still at the wide outside. On this flat course, in this going, with this tempo, the tactical verdict is clear: hold-up and prominent closers who settle kindly, travel without fuss, and have the stamina to sustain a run through the final two furlongs hold the structural advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the five front-runners set a fierce early gallop that burns them out, leaving the race to those settled in midfield or behind.
scenarios.body: Pride Of Toledo and the pace contingent will have torn into each other through the first three furlongs on soft ground, leaving the late-movers with a collapsing target as they enter the Doncaster straight; the stamina emphasis rewards horses who have conserved energy and can sustain a strong, progressive finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If one or two pace horses break clear early and the tempo becomes controlled enough to reward a prominent, well-positioned runner.
scenarios.body: Should the pace fracture — with some front-runners losing interest or being outpaced — a single pace-setter could dictate a more managed gallop, suiting a prominent racer who travels smoothly just behind and picks off a tiring leader in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Proves Resilient
scenarios.trigger: If the strongest front-runner establishes a rhythm and the soft ground paradoxically slows the pace enough to allow a well-backed pace horse to sustain its effort.
scenarios.body: On occasions at Doncaster, a well-handled front-runner can dictate off a moderate but consistent gallop on soft ground, holding on as closers fail to quicken sufficiently through the testing surface.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide Draw Outsiders Exploit Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the internal battle for position causes interference and traffic issues for midfield horses, allowing horses from wider draws to skirt the trouble.
scenarios.body: Fern Clyde and Fasthope, though displaced from their natural prominent positions, could benefit if the inner bunches of front-runners tangle or check, freeing up a clear run on the outside; however, both are racing out of their natural role here, which tempers confidence materially.

watchPoints.text: Bear Lee (draw 1) and Tumishi (draw 2) are in danger of being severely bottled up on the inner rail if the five confirmed front-runners dominate the rail early — watch for both to be checked or unable to quicken when asked.

Innichen's sole soft-ground run produced a 19th-of-19 finish, which is an extreme red flag; if the going description is correctly soft and not merely riding fast, he may disappoint significantly despite his strong good-ground form.

Sir Sirius returns from 78 days off and will be competing for a prominent position from stall 13 in a pace-heavy field — watch for him to be outpaced early and drop away, rendering the strong pace even more unsustainable for the horses who do make the running.

Beresford Gap is ridden by Oisin Murphy but returns from 50 days off as a front-runner in a race with four other confirmed pace horses — watch for Murphy to either sacrifice position early or for the horse to be vulnerable in the final furlong if he has been asked hard questions throughout.

Launch Sequence carries a first-time headgear flag — if the application sharpens him, K R Burke's 13/42 14-day form and James Doyle in the saddle from a clean stall-7 draw gives this horse an each-way profile that the market may not fully account for.

runners_data.name: Almekarem
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's 4yo has winning form on soft going (1W1P sim-going) and ran well over 10f on soft last time; midfield style suits this strongly-run race ideally and the Prescott yard targets these conditions precisely.

runners_data.name: Amidst The Chaos
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with a win over 12f on Tapeta on the figures but no soft-ground win; Rowan Scott takes the ride and the horse's style means it will be last to enter the argument, requiring a lot to go right in a 19-runner field.

runners_data.name: Optician
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard selection at low confidence; won over 12f on soft (1W1P sim-going) and ran 2nd over 10f on good last time, and this track/trip/going combination is exactly where Michael Herrington's 6yo has shown its best; 5lb claimer Conor Whiteley keeps costs low and the midfield style sits perfectly in the expected shape.

runners_data.name: Without Compromise
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who shaped well when 2nd over 10f on good earlier this season; Cam Hardie knows the horse and it handles this trip, though it has no recorded soft-ground win and faces the risk of being dragged into a pace battle it cannot sustain.

runners_data.name: Reveur
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's 3yo is lightly raced with going entirely unknown and returns after 126 days off — significant questions unanswered before a 19-runner handicap; Daniel Tudhope adds class in the saddle but the horse carries too many uncertainties to assess with confidence.

runners_data.name: Everyoneknowsadave
runners_data.note: Jessica Macey's 4yo has been placed prominently at this trip on multiple occasions and arrives on the back of a win over 10f on Tapeta; Sean Levey is a significant booking and the horse's ability to sit just off a hot pace makes it a natural beneficiary of Scenario B.

runners_data.name: His Finest Hour
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason rides for a small stable with no recent winners; the horse has placed twice on soft ground over 10f and 11f but its prominent style means it risks getting caught up in the early pace battle rather than sitting sweetly off it.

runners_data.name: Director's Cut
runners_data.note: One of the confirmed front-runners, last won over 8f on Tapeta for Ross Burdon; returns after 74 days off and steps up sharply in trip to 12f on soft going — both the layoff and the distance rise are concerns for a horse that is asked to set or fight for a strong pace.

runners_data.name: Canvas
runners_data.note: A confirmed lead-seeker who is flagged as prone to fading in the finish — a dangerous combination when the early pace will be strong; soft-going record (2nd on soft) suggests it handles the surface, but the fade tendency in a truly-run race over 12f is a material risk.

runners_data.name: Something Splendid
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard danger and a compelling profile: Tom Marquand takes the ride, Peter Chapple-Hyam's 4yo won on soft last time at 10f and has two soft-ground wins from six similar-going runs; a prominent, confident ride from just off the pace suits the expected shape well.

runners_data.name: Newtown Duke
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' 5yo is fitted with a tongue-tie and has placed twice on soft including a 3rd over 12f on soft; returns after 90 days off, which tempers enthusiasm, though the hold-up style and course form over this trip are both relevant.

runners_data.name: Amancio
runners_data.note: Faye Bramley's 5yo has two wins on soft going including over 9f and 17f, showing remarkable versatility; tongue-tie applied and the horse has placed multiple times in similar conditions — prominent style over 12f on soft is a solid fit and the yard has been active recently.

runners_data.name: Highland Olly
runners_data.note: One of the confirmed pace-setters; has never won beyond 9f and arrives off a career mostly spent over 7-9f — the step to 12f on soft ground while setting a strong gallop looks likely to find the horse out in the final stages despite tactical freshness after 12 days.

runners_data.name: On The Inlet
runners_data.note: Jack Doughty's 3yo front-runner won over 7f on Tapeta before three unplaced runs; has no soft-ground win and has not won beyond 7f, meaning the combination of trip, surface, and strong early pace test is a significant ask.

runners_data.name: Fans Favourite
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride on Hugo Palmer's 3yo who has won three times on soft including twice at 10f — the hold-up style, high-class jockey booking, and excellent soft-ground strike rate (3W3P from 9 similar-going runs) make this a well-suited runner for the expected race shape.

runners_data.name: Illy's Roo
runners_data.note: David Egan rides Gemma Tutty's 3yo who has not won beyond 8f and has no soft-ground win; hold-up style is fine for the shape but the trip extension and surface are both concerns, and Egan's booking is the most compelling argument in its favour.

runners_data.name: Spirit Genie
runners_data.note: Jason Hart's 6yo won over 8f on good recently but has been well beaten on soft before; tongue-tie and bit fitted, and while the hold-up style suits the race shape, the absence of a soft-ground win and the step to 12f make this a marginal runner at best.

runners_data.name: Ziata
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne's 3yo is a confirmed front-runner with five soft-ground runs but no win on the surface; has not won beyond 10f and is likely to be a pacemaker rather than a contender, with the low OR of 68 reflecting limited scope.

runners_data.name: Naples
runners_data.note: P J McDonald takes the ride but Steph Hollinshead's 4yo has not won since finishing 3rd on soft and has been well beaten in recent runs including 21st over 8f; hold-up style is the right shape but the form is deeply uninspiring and the horse looks outclassed.

races.paceDynamic: Highland Olly, On The Inlet, Director's Cut, Canvas, and Ziata all want to be on or near the lead, guaranteeing a strongly-run race from the outset over 1m2f on Good to Soft ground at Doncaster. With five confirmed front-runners scrapping for positions from the off, the early pace will be genuine and unrelenting, meaning there is almost no chance of this becoming a slowly-run tactical affair. The soft-ground stamina demands compound the attrition — horses who exert energy fighting for lead position early are likely to be vulnerable in the final two furlongs. This race shape firmly favours off-the-pace midfield-to-hold-up runners who can travel within themselves, conserve energy through the early battle, and produce a sustained late run down Doncaster's flat, unforgiving straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the five front-runners burn each other out setting a genuine gallop, leaving the midfield and hold-up horses with a clean passage to strike late.
scenarios.body: The fractious early battle for the lead on soft ground drains the front-runners entering the straight, opening the race for those who settled in mid-division; Doncaster's long, flat run-in rewards sustained galloping types with a late surge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent-style runners sits just off the hot pace without fighting for the lead, times their move perfectly, and pounces before the hold-up horses engage.
scenarios.body: Something Splendid or Everyoneknowsadave settles in second or third gear behind the frantic early leaders and inherits a decisive advantage turning for home; the pace in front does enough damage to the true front-runners while the prominent stalker is never out of a comfortable rhythm.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Gallops Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace fractures early with one horse — most likely Director's Cut or On The Inlet — establishing a clear lead and controlling a steady enough tempo to conserve enough to hold on.
scenarios.body: In a scenario where the early battle resolves quickly and one lead horse escapes cleanly, the soft ground paradoxically rewards a horse who gets into a long, rhythmic stride unchallenged rather than fighting rivals; the remaining front-runners having burned themselves out become pacemakers rather than threats.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Produces Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the crowded early pace causes interference, checks, or a muddling tempo, allowing an unconsidered hold-up runner to produce a big-field handicap special.
scenarios.body: A messy race where pace judgement collapses could see a horse like Spirit Genie or Amidst The Chaos emerge from the chaos with a clean run at the field; big-field handicaps on soft ground over this trip have a habit of producing at least one eyecatcher who threads through when others have flattered to deceive.

watchPoints.text: Fans Favourite (Oisin Murphy, Hugo Palmer) carries a 3W3P soft-ground record into a race shape that suits hold-up horses — watch for Murphy tracking the field before delivering a sustained challenge in the straight.

Something Splendid (Tom Marquand, Peter Chapple-Hyam) won last time on soft and is the Strand Scorecard's named danger — a prominent, controlled ride just off the pace war could see it hit the line strongest of all.

The five-way battle for the lead involving Highland Olly, On The Inlet, Director's Cut, Canvas, and Ziata risks producing interference and checks in the first two furlongs — any hold-up runner who suffers a check or is blocked early could have its race ruined before it starts.

Director's Cut returns after 74 days off and steps up sharply in trip on soft ground while expected to set the pace — if the horse fades rapidly from the 3f pole it could cause interference and impede runners mounting their challenges.

Optician (Conor Whiteley 5lb claim, Michael Herrington) is the Strand Scorecard's top selection at low confidence — watch whether the 5lb claim proves decisive in a tight finish, as the horse's 1W1P soft-going record over 12f is a genuine asset.
